notes:
User is building a gaming setup and wants recommendations for competitive FPS games, especially Apex Legends. They are considering a SteelSeries Rival 600 mouse and are interested in its TrueMove3 12,000 DPI sensor; this choice is still tentative. They have a new keyboard already, though its model is unknown.

For a headset, the user is strongly leaning toward the HyperX Cloud II for its comfort and microphone quality, but is concerned that its virtual 7.1 surround sound may sound inaccurate or “wonky” in some games. They asked whether that could be a dealbreaker for competitive Apex. Their preference appears to favor comfort and mic quality even if spatial audio is imperfect; practical advice would be to use stereo rather than virtual surround, since stereo is commonly used competitively and virtual processing can be less consistent.

The user plays Apex Legends frequently with friends and has upgraded their long-term progression goal from level 100 to level 150. They are determined to reach level 150 eventually, but do not want leveling to dominate a weekend gaming session with friends; for that weekend, they have decided to prioritize fun over strict leveling. They nevertheless plan to complete daily and weekly challenges to earn additional experience, stay motivated, and track progress. They want to balance challenge completion with normal gameplay without becoming stressed, sacrificing enjoyment, or burning out.

User is interested in concrete gameplay-skill advice and team communication. Future guidance should cover map awareness, positioning, cover, rotations, team role synergy, weapon and ammo management, mobility, ability use, crosshair placement, target tracking, micro-flicks, recoil/first-burst control, movement drills, reviewing deathcams, watching/reviewing stronger players thoughtfully, and deliberate practice. For communication, advise concise enemy/contact callouts, clear and useful pings, sharing plans, positive teamwork, and post-match review. Communication should support—not distract from—combat awareness.

For aim improvement, emphasize a consistent warmup and drills, appropriate mouse-sensitivity adjustments rather than raw DPI alone, and Apex-specific weapons/Range. Do not overstate that watching one pro or repeatedly increasing DPI is necessary. Avoid questionable advice such as claiming Apex audio is “forgiving” or prioritizing visuals over audio; both visual and audio cues matter in competitive play.
